title: One progress line: stretch bands, scene windows and a speed-capped clock
summary: Scroll inside a `900svh` sticky track (Lenis on the shared ticker) is a raw 0–1 folded through a piecewise-linear map where two stretch bands cost more scroll (`.24–.36 × 2`, `.62–.72 × 1.5`, overlapping bands discarded); a clock follows that target at most `K × dt / FILM_SECONDS` per frame (`4`, `14 s`) so a flick cannot skip a beat; five scene windows of generated three.js geometry switched on half-way into the window before and off half-way into the next (`visible` toggled, never disposed), with a per-window `dropPrevAt` override; a rail drawn from the same tables; one settled frame per beat under reduced motion and static
variants: native scroll through Lenis on a sticky stage (this, default)
virtual float: feed the same raw value from a wheel-driven float instead of scrollY (see gl-virtual-scroll-camera)
per-window hooks: run enter / leave callbacks on the same toggles to start and stop each scene's own loop or audio stem
